agent.name: Organizational Adoption Agent
agent.specialty: Organizational readiness to absorb govern and sustain a specified application

analytical_question: Can the constructed financial-services organization responsibly learn from, then sustain, supervised agentic chart review within a four-week planning window without overriding the team's current DEFER decision?
general_et_finding: Agentic AI here combines a language model, model-selected tools, observations, permissions and human stopping authority for bounded multistep work; it is not equivalent to a standalone model or chart plugin. Organizational adoption requires named oversight, competent reviewers, controlled inputs and tools, reliable handoffs, incident response and continuing support. NIST AI RMF 1.0 (S1) and GenAI Profile (S2) offer voluntary governance and monitoring practices, not certification, company evidence or legal rules. The C3 implementation framework distinguishes a feasibility proof of concept, subsequent comparative value evidence and organizational acceptance. General system characteristics and application feasibility remain unchanged between these profiles; organizational capacity changes what can responsibly be attempted.
application_finding: For supervised chart review, a bounded agent would use read-only tools to compare chart labels, denominators, visual encodings and written claims against approved source tables, then provide traceable draft corrections to a named human reviewer. The reviewer must independently verify source lineage and interpretation and explicitly sign off before publication; the agent never publishes or makes financial/customer decisions. A feasibility PoC would test whether the read-only chain, provenance, error capture and stopping controls function on public/synthetic examples. A separate matched comparison against current manual/deterministic review would then be necessary to determine accuracy, severe-error incidence, reviewer effort, total support burden and incremental net benefit. Neither case supplies these performance or value outcomes; technology/application fit remains UNVALIDATED and comparative net advantage UNKNOWN.
organization_specific_finding: Overall judgment: readiness for desk-based assessment of an isolated learning option is limited but plausible; organizational readiness for an actual agent PoC is NOT ESTABLISHED, and routine use is NOT ESTABLISHED. Eight domains: (1) Leadership/sponsorship—no named committed sponsor or project authorization is evidenced; conservative posture is not opposition or consent. (2) Skills/training—experienced BI analysts provide chart/domain knowledge, but agent-tool, provenance, escalation and reviewer competency are unverified. (3) Workflow/process—existing chart review and required human publication sign-off provide a starting control; documented handoff, exception queue, fallback, acceptance and support process are not evidenced. (4) Infrastructure/data—established BI source tables exist, but approved external-model route, isolated agent environment, validation cases, sensitive-data permission and production integrations are not supplied. (5) Resources/budget—reviewer time, engineering support, recurring spend and contingency capacity are unknown. (6) Governance/risk—human authority is required, but access approval, logging, incident escalation, model-risk review and rehearsed recovery are not evidenced. (7) Culture/change—analyst experience cannot establish acceptance, psychological safety or change readiness. (8) Operating ownership—no named accountable agent operator, service owner, backup or maintenance escalation is evidenced. These are evidence gaps, not demonstrated organizational failures. High-consequence report distribution makes a missing gate material, even though drafts are reversible.

evidence.claim: Established BI tables, experienced analysts, human sign-off requirement and absent trial authorization are case premises
evidence.notes: They support a review baseline, not AI readiness or permission.

evidence.claim: Team baseline is DEFER for unapproved chart-agent trial; manual/deterministic review remains
evidence.notes: Not a measured experiment or independent organizational observation.

evidence.claim: All eight readiness domains and owner/gap assessment are required
evidence.notes: An analytical rubric rather than firm evidence.

evidence.claim: Separate feasibility, value and acceptance, and design a conditional PoC
evidence.notes: No checklist score or demonstrated feasibility.

evidence.claim: Governance, trained roles, monitoring and recovery are relevant controls
evidence.source_or_reference: S1 NIST AI 100-1; S2 NIST AI 600-1
evidence.notes: No regulatory determination or claim of implemented control.

evidence.claim: Compatibility, trialability and observability are useful local questions
evidence.notes: No inference that the organization has adopted the technology.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: No proof that unknown sponsor, reviewer capacity, budget or cultural acceptance is absent; do not describe these gaps as failure.
No approved environment or agent trial; desk research permission cannot be treated as execution approval.
No representative agent outputs, matched baseline, severe-error measurements, support costs or routine-release decision.
S1/S2 are voluntary frameworks; supplied course/team artifacts are teaching evidence, not firsthand company outcomes.
confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence in the narrow judgment that an actual trial is presently unauthorized and readiness unverified because those are explicit case premises. Moderate confidence that BI experience and required sign-off are useful starting points. Low confidence in whether the unknown sponsorship, capacity, competencies and operating arrangements could be remedied within four weeks; no numerical readiness score is justified.
value_opportunity_implication: Potential benefit is reduced repetitive checking with traceable corrections; no reduction is demonstrated. Analyst verification and incident handling could cancel apparent efficiency. Compare agent-assisted review with the best current manual/deterministic baseline using matched cases, including misleading denominators and invented claims; report total human and platform effort as well as errors, not just model output speed.
risk_governance_implication: No sensitive or production data, autonomous publication, external model routing or downstream decisions should be inferred permitted. Prior to any future PoC, security and model-risk owners should approve isolation, tool permissions, logging, source lineage, data restrictions, human veto, incident stop and manual recovery. A named publication reviewer remains accountable for release. A documented role requirement alone does not appoint or fund an owner.
recommendation_management_implication: Preserve DEFER and current deterministic/manual controls. During the four-week planning window: first, a reporting executive should decide whether to sponsor a scoped request; model risk, compliance and security should document possible gate criteria, not imply approval. Second, reporting management and BI reviewers should map handoffs, errors, source checks, training needs and acceptance concerns. Third, finance and IT should assess protected reviewer time, environment, budget and support ownership; appoint an accountable operating owner plus deputy only if leadership authorizes. Conditional PoC design, NOT execution: purpose is feasibility of supervised read-only traceable chart checks; scope is a four-week isolated public/synthetic-only test with no publication or sensitive inputs; proposed roles are sponsor, BI reviewers, platform maintainer, risk/security approvers and independent human sign-off. Execution gate requires explicit charter, approved environment and permissions, staff capacity, test set, incident plan and stop authority. Track source traceability, denominator/claim defects, severity, human override, completion time, training load, incidents and fallback success. Stop on unauthorized access, provenance failure, uncontained serious error or absent reviewer capacity; review findings before any value trial. A feasibility result alone cannot release routine use.
change_monitoring_triggers: At four-week review, re-evaluate only on documented authorization, sponsor/operator appointment, approved isolation, competency evidence and resourcing.
If any data/tool permission changes or severe error emerges, halt any future authorized test and seek risk-owner review.
At quarter-end, assess recurring staff cost, change acceptance, incident handling, backup coverage and updated matched value evidence; no automatic deployment trigger.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Identify actual willing sponsor, authorized decision body and whether any isolated trial may be requested.
Obtain named service owner/deputy, staff time, budget, reviewer training and workflow acceptance evidence.
Require security/model-risk approved routes, provenance/logging/recovery design and representative matched baseline before feasibility/value conclusions.
